svg.title: Cell processes
svg.desc: CHROMOSOMES & GENES: The nucleus contains chromosomes made of DNA. Each chromosome carries many genes. Body-cell chromosomes normally occur in pairs. DNA copying produces two joined identical copies of each chromosome. A copied X shape is one chromosome with two sister chromatids. 1. GROW & COPY DNA: Before mitosis, the cell grows. The number of structures, such as ribosomes and mitochondria, increases. DNA replicates to make two copies of each chromosome. DNA amount doubles; chromosome number has not doubled. The joined copies will separate during mitosis. 2. MITOSIS: The joined chromosome copies separate. One complete set is pulled to each end of the cell. The nucleus divides. DNA copying happened before this stage. Mitosis maintains chromosome number; it does not halve it. 3. CELL DIVISION: The cytoplasm and membrane divide. Two genetically identical daughter cells form, with the same chromosome number as the parent. Needed for growth, development, repair and replacement: for example, healing skin. Bacteria divide by binary fission, not mitosis. HUMAN STEM CELLS: An undifferentiated cell can divide and produce cells that differentiate. Embryonic stem cells can form most types of human cell. Adult bone marrow stem cells form a more limited range, including blood cells. The source affects which cells can be produced. MEDICAL USES: Potentially replace damaged cells, such as insulin-producing cells in diabetes or nerve cells in paralysis. Therapeutic cloning: an embryo is produced with the patient's genes. Its stem cells can provide genetically matched tissue, which the patient's immune system does not reject. Potential treatments are not guaranteed cures. BENEFITS, RISKS & ETHICS: Benefit → replacement cells may repair damaged tissue. Risks include transfer of viral infection and uncontrolled division. Some people have ethical or religious objections, including to embryo destruction. Others consider treatment benefits more important. Evaluate the source, benefits and risks, then give a reasoned judgement. PLANT MERISTEMS: Meristems produce cells that can differentiate into any type of plant cell throughout life. They can produce plant clones quickly and economically. Clone rare plants → help prevent extinction. Clone useful crop plants → many identical plants with features such as disease resistance. Plant meristems produce plant cells; human stem cells produce human cells.
